quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to cars in traffic?

options.text: Much less distance
Less distance
The same distance
More distance

questions.correctAnswerText: The same distance
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars.

questions.question: You are stopped for a moving traffic violation. You are wearing a helmet and are over 18 years old. What happens?

options.text: You will not get a ticket.
You will get a ticket, but have 30 extra days to pay.
You will get a ticket, but $8 of the fine will be waived.
You will get a ticket, but it will not appear on your record.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will get a ticket, but $8 of the fine will be waived.
questions.explanation: In Utah, riders over 18 are not required to wear helmets. However, if you wear a helmet and get a moving violation ticket, $8 of the fine will be waived to encourage helmet use.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give them?

options.text: Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet to help you focus on riding. They should get on only after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Why should you NOT move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting in too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut in too early.
It encourages the passing driver to pass more quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut in too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: Your front wheel starts to skid. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride it out.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then re-engage it.
Release the front brake and press the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then re-engage it.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up, release the front brake completely right away. Then re-apply it smoothly.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps drivers see you best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Bright colors like red, orange, yellow, or green help drivers see you. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: You are about to pass a vehicle on the left. Where should you position your motorcycle in your lane?

options.text: On the right side so they see you in their side mirror.
On the left side to see better and be more visible.
In the center so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave back and forth to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side to see better and be more visible.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle on the left side of your lane to improve your view and make yourself more visible. Check mirrors and turn your head before changing lanes.

questions.question: How should you pack cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Avoid placing items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag. Load cargo over or in front of the rear axle. Placing cargo behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: You cannot avoid hitting an object in the road. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting it.
Slow down before hitting it.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before hitting it.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible before impact. Try to hit the object at a 90-degree angle. Keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle before impact.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is too close to the car ahead.
Someone is sitting in a parked car's driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn to alert other drivers or pedestrians who may move into your path. Do not use it for attention. It is good to horn before passing a nearby vehicle or pedestrian.

questions.question: When your motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should reduce pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.
Lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel has more grip. This means you can press the front brake harder.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, you should:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth to free it. If that doesn't work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for riders under 18 years old.
Required for riders under 21 years old.
Required only for riders with licenses less than two years old.
Never required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for riders under 18 years old.
questions.explanation: In Utah, all motorcycle riders and passengers under 18 must wear helmets. Helmets are strongly recommended for all riders.

questions.question: Who should set the pace for a group of riders?

options.text: The leader
The riders just behind the leader
The rider in back
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider in back
questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

options.text: Three times
Four times
Five times
Six times

questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to get a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When stopping, it is best to:

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.
Only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: Apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight moves forward, use more front brake and less rear brake. Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often alcohol is consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: The three main factors that affect BAC are the amount of alcohol, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. Sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have an effect.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is accomplished by:

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?

options.text: Follow me
Slow down
Speed up
Exit

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals are used to communicate in group riding. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: At night, what is the minimum following distance a motorcyclist should keep?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to notice if the vehicle stops and to slow down or stop safely.

questions.question: What is the safest way to cross angled railroad tracks?

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.
Cross at a 45-degree angle.
Cross at a 90-degree angle.
Cross at a fast speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: The safest way is to go straight in your lane. Turning to cross at a right angle can be dangerous because it may push you into another lane.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Change your path as needed.
Use the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve and then straighten out. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve itself.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The near side of the lane is safer.
You will feel more wind blast from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action first, then the other.
Do both at the same time and brake hard.
Do both at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.
Do neither action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need traction to swerve safely, so do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action and then the other.
